clauses.current_legal_basis: The U.S. Code release point 119-121 prints Executive Order 11448 in force as amended by Executive Order 12312 and by Executive Order 13286 section 61, as a note to 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57, and section 1 of the printed order reads: for award by the Secretary of a Military Department or the Secretary of Homeland Security with regard to the Coast Guard when not operating as a service in the Navy, to any member of the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation.
clauses.reason: EO 12312 restates section 1 of EO 11448 so that the medal may be awarded to members of the armed forces of friendly foreign nations; the restated text named the Secretary of Transportation for the Coast Guard. EO 13286 section 61 (held text, American Presidency Project transcription, with section 92: This order shall become effective on March 1, 2003) strikes the Secretary of Transportation in section 1 and inserts the Secretary of Homeland Security in lieu thereof. Before the amendment the restated section 1 named the Secretary of Transportation with regard to the Coast Guard; after it, the same words name the Secretary of Homeland Security, and the foreign-member clause is unchanged. Under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling the amendment is a later event and the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends. The Code note to 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 prints EO 11448 as amended by both orders, so the clause is operative as of 2026-10-14.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12312 of July 2, 1981 (46 FR 35251, July 8, 1981) was read in full from the held Federal Register original (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12312.txt, PDF page 9). It is a single command that restates section 1 of Executive Order 11448 of January 16, 1969, the Meritorious Service Medal order, so that the medal can be awarded to members of the armed forces of friendly foreign nations. Under the owner ruling on strike-and-insert and restated sections (2026-10-21), the clause continues, as amended, as long as the parent order continues. The parent order is in force: the U.S. Code release point 119-121 prints Executive Order 11448 as amended by EO 12312 and by EO 13286 section 61 as a note to 10 U.S.C. subtitle A, part II, chapter 57. The one later change is EO 13286 section 61, which strikes the Secretary of Transportation in section 1 and inserts the Secretary of Homeland Security; it takes effect March 1, 2003 under section 92 of EO 13286. The held Federal Register catalog and held-text number searches show no other amendment, revocation or supersession of EO 12312. Bounded searches read for coverage before use: current-law:usc covers the U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted after that date and on or before 2026-10-14 are not reflected); current-law:ecfr covers the eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk XML; later-events:ofr_catalog covers Office of the Federal Register disposition notes of 6942 catalog records (1937 onward) plus operative sentences in 16784 saved order texts. These are machine leads, not independent review; the two-week gap in the U.S. Code edition is disclosed here.

savings.reason: The order contains no savings, transition or pending-action language; it only restates section 1 of EO 11448, and no held source shows any action that depended on the pre-1981 wording alone.
